Problem: Given an arithmetic-geometric sequence ${a_{n}}$ with the sum of the first $n$ terms denoted as $S_{n}$, and $S_{2}=1$, $S_{4}=3$, find the value of $S_{6}$. Express your answer as a single integer.

This formula is a pure geometric sequence; an arithmetic-geometric sequence must include an arithmetic factor, such as a_n=(a+(n-1)d)r^{n-1}, so the definition is incorrect.
Replace it with the correct general term for an arithmetic-geometric sequence before applying the sum formulas.
